context: Fix two pre-existing load-sensitive flaky test clusters that failed roughly one full suite run in two, a different test each time, and passed in isolation and on clean main.
root_causes: tests/unit/test_kimi_login.py coordinates async tasks with asyncio.wait_for budgets of 0.1s. These are not latency assertions: each waits for an event that either fires or does not, so a tight budget only buys sensitivity to CPU contention, and whichever test lost the scheduler race failed.

test_real_headroom_smoke_uses_memory_only_state invoked the REAL Headroom compressor with a hard-coded 5s timeout and then asserted the outcome was a success. Under a loaded run the compressor exceeds that and fails open with reason 'timeout', so the test failed for a reason unrelated to the property it guards.
evidence: Observed across the whole OpenCode Go slice series: a different test failed each time, always in one of these two files.
Reproduced deliberately: with the fix stashed, 2 of 4 loaded full-suite runs failed; with it applied, 3 of 3 were clean under the same conditions.
Running the two affected files alone under external CPU load does NOT reproduce it; the contention comes from the full suite itself.
Mutation proof that the waits are still load bearing: making the login task never run fails the suite at the new budget rather than passing.
solutions: Replace the test-side coordination budgets with one named constant at 10s, leaving the timeout_seconds config of the code under test untouched.

Make the headroom smoke test outcome agnostic: accept fail-open reasons, since the invariant it exists for is that the real path writes nothing under HOME, and raise its timeout so a fail-open means a genuine hang rather than ordinary contention.
acceptance_criteria: Three consecutive loaded full-suite runs pass.
The affected files still pass in isolation.
The async waits still fail when an event genuinely never fires, proven by mutation.
No timeout_seconds value belonging to the code under test is changed.
No test is skipped, deselected or marked xfail.
legacy_risk_reason: loosening a test-side wait can hide a real regression, so the change is paired with a mutation proof that the waits still gate on the event actually firing
